I read the whole file and looked for nontrivial reasoning that is repeated across proofs. I did not open the imported files, because no candidate looked strong enough to need a shared lemma.

The repeated pieces I found are all short.
- The measurability of `{y | r ≤ nndist x y}` and of its indicator of `edist x y ^ p.toReal` appears in `setLIntegral_edist_rpow_le_of_isFrechetBarycenter_sum_smul_dirac` as `hA` and `hfind`. It appears again in `exists_lintegral_setLIntegral_edist_rpow_le` as `hA` and `hf`. Each use is one or two lines of term-mode API composition (`measurableSet_le`, `.indicator`).
- Both `isCompact_closure_range_of_isFrechetBarycenter` and `exists_isFrechetBarycenter` unpack `∃ s, ∀ᵐ μ ∂P n, μ ∈ s` and call `exists_eq_sum_smul_dirac_of_ae_mem_finset`. This is a thin wrapper around an existing lemma.
- Several proofs share the `Fact (p ≠ ∞)` and nonemptiness boilerplate. That is routine setup.

The main arguments are not duplicated.
- The pointwise tail bound is proved once, in the private lemma.
- The integrated version uses a joint law Γ.
- The mixture-kernel convergence argument appears once.
- The compactness and subsequence steps each appear once.

A shared helper for the measurability facts would not be a substantial improvement under this rubric. I found no justified finding.
